title: Informal EU Defence Ministers Meet in Wicklow, Ireland — Ukraine Air Defence, Hormuz, Hybrid Threats
detail: EU defence ministers met at Druids Glen, County Wicklow, on August 31–September 1, hosted by Ireland's Minister for Defence Helen McEntee as part of Ireland's Council Presidency, together with High Representative Kaja Kallas. Kallas called air defence capabilities the most urgent need, describing July–August as the 'deadliest months' for Ukrainian civilians in the war, and urged member states — some of whom hold interceptor missile stockpiles nearing expiry — to hand them over; she reported 'unfortunately no concrete success' securing fresh pledges from Greece and Spain. Ministers also discussed maintaining freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz without tolls or fees, protection of critical undersea infrastructure, and space defence. Kallas warned Russia is hitting Europe with 'a wave of increasingly kinetic hybrid attacks' meant to intimidate Ukraine's supporters. McEntee said Ireland has raised defence spending 43% and intends to join the EU's SAFE defence-investment instrument, and confirmed Ireland is 'absolutely' willing to contribute to a prospective new EU mission in Lebanon once UNIFIL's mandate expires.

title: Eurozone Inflation Jumps to 3.3% in August as Energy Prices Surge
detail: Eurostat's flash estimate put euro area annual HICP inflation at 3.3% in August 2026, up sharply from 2.9% in July and the highest reading since September 2023. Energy prices rose 14.3% year-on-year (up from 10.3% in July), driven by global oil and gas price pressure linked to the war in Iran and disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz; services inflation eased to 3.0% from 3.3%, and core inflation (excluding energy and food) slipped to 2.4%. Non-energy industrial goods rose 1.2% (from 0.9%) and food/alcohol/tobacco held at 1.2%. Spain posted the highest national rate among major economies at 4.5%. The reading reinforces market expectations the ECB Governing Council will raise its deposit facility rate by 25bp, to 2.5%, at its September 10 meeting.
